newsitem.title: USA: Gore launches anti-crime drive for public housing.
newsitem.headline: Gore launches anti-crime drive for public housing.

text.p: The Clinton administration launched a drive Thursday to protect public housing residents from drugs and crime in 13 cities.
"Today, we get tough and help families," Vice President Al Gore said at a ceremony to showcase a new crimefighting strategy.
It builds on a year-old programme that targeted six of the cities with the most violent public housing: San Francisco, Philadelphia, Chicago, Detroit, New Orleans and Washington.
The seven new cities added were Newark, New Jersey; Kansas City, Missouri; Boston, Massachussetts; Atlanta, Georgia; Greensboro, North Carolina; Memphis, Tennessee; and Gary, Indiana.
A White House statment said the program's first prong would step up law enforcement activities in the 13 cities, which it termed "the worst of the worst" for troubled public housing.

Also called for were tailor-made, community-driven programmes to keep criminals out. The Department of Housing and Urban Development will provide $250 million in grants this year to support community-base strategies.
A further $20 million will be earmarked next year to strengthen HUD's Operation Safe Home, a crime-fighting programme aimed at coordinating law enforcement at the federal, state and local levels.
"This new four-part strategy stops the criminals, protects the law-abiding citiznes in public housing, and will make our neighbourhoods safe for children," Gore said.

HUD Secretary Andrew Cuomo told the gathering of law enforcement personnel and community activists from around the country that eliminating drugs would be the single "greatest improvement" to public housing.
Attorney General Janet Reno said the programme would build on the declining U.S. crime rate, which fell last year for the fifth year in a row.
"Those who make their homes in our nation's public housing deserve to live without fear, like every American," she said.
